content.text:
Country A: 120 laptops or 20 bicycles. So 1 laptop costs 20/120 = 1/6 of a bicycle.
Country B: 1 laptop costs 30/60 = 1/2 of a bicycle. Country A's cost is lower, so A has the comparative advantage in laptops.
For part C, the bicycle intercept doubles from 20 to 40 and the laptop intercept stays at 120, so the curve pivots outward.
For part D, B has the comparative advantage in bicycles. Its cost is 2 laptops per bicycle, compared with 6 for A. The terms of trade need to fall between 1/6 and 1/2 bicycle per laptop.

answers.brief_reasoning: 20 bicycles / 120 laptops = 1/6 bicycle per laptop.
answers.final_answer: 1/6 (about 0.17) bicycle per laptop

answers.brief_reasoning: A gives up 1/6 bicycle per laptop and B gives up 1/2. A's cost is lower.
answers.final_answer: Country A

answers.brief_reasoning: Draw a straight-line PPC with laptops on the horizontal axis, running from 120 laptops to 20 bicycles. Then draw a new line, PPC2, that pivots out on the bicycle axis to 40 and keeps the laptop intercept at 120.
answers.final_answer: PPC1 has intercepts at 120 laptops and 20 bicycles. PPC2 has intercepts at 120 laptops and 40 bicycles. It pivots outward along the vertical axis only.

answers.brief_reasoning: Each country specializes in the good with the lower opportunity cost and trades for the other.
answers.final_answer: A specializes in laptops, where its opportunity cost is lowest. B specializes in bicycles, where its opportunity cost is 2 laptops per bicycle versus 6 for A. They trade at terms between 1/6 and 1/2 bicycle per laptop, for example 1 bicycle for 3 laptops. That way each country gets the other good more cheaply than it could make it at home, and both can consume outside their own PPCs.
